candidate_causes.cause_description: A pre-existing internal obstruction of the bypass path left the bypass effectively closed although the handle indicated open. The packet does not characterize the obstruction; it could be foreign material, debris, or a valve internal failure. Start-up therefore proceeded without an available bypass flow path, resulting in internal damage to V-001.

evidence_against.relevance: The obstruction was identified only after the event. Its presence before start-up and its origin and composition are not established.
No independent pre-start-up record of actual bypass flow exists, so it cannot be shown that the bypass was blocked at the moment of start-up.

evidence_for.relevance: Post-event inspection found an internal obstruction in the bypass path with the handle in the indicated open position. This directly provides a mechanism for an ineffective bypass independent of operator action.
The time-stamped witness record shows the handle was moved to open before start-up. An ineffective bypass therefore requires a non-operator explanation such as a physical blockage.
Damage occurred even though the bypass step was recorded as completed. This is consistent with the flow path being unavailable despite correct line-up.
The observed damage matches the HAZOP-referenced consequence of a start-up deviation at V-001.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Latent procedural weakness in the sole safeguard. The commissioning procedure and checklist confirmed the bypass step by handle position and sign-off, without requiring independent verification of actual bypass flow before start-up. This allowed a blocked flow path to go undetected. It is a contributing cause that coexists with C1.

evidence_against.relevance: Absence of a verification record does not prove the procedure lacked a verification requirement, or that no verification was performed.
The procedure content is not supplied, so the specific gap is inferred rather than documented. A procedural gap is only an enabling condition and needs a physical cause such as C1 to produce damage.

evidence_for.relevance: The checklist records the step as completed, but no independent verification of actual bypass flow is available. This indicates the safeguard confirmed the action rather than the outcome.
Handle position proved to be an unreliable indicator of flow-path availability, so a check based on handle position could not detect the obstruction.
The commissioning procedure is the only listed safeguard, and the HAZOP consequence occurred with it in place.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Alternative initiating mechanism: the damage to V-001 arose from another start-up deviation or process condition not documented in the packet. Under this explanation the bypass obstruction is secondary or coincidental rather than causal; for example, debris from damaged internals or accessories may have lodged in the bypass after the event.

evidence_against.relevance: The obstruction lies specifically in the bypass path whose line-up is the step at issue. A causal link is more parsimonious than coincidence or deposition after the event.
No evidence item identifies any other deviating start-up step or abnormal process condition. Nothing links the obstruction's composition to V-001 internals.

evidence_for.relevance: The obstruction was found only at post-event inspection, which does not establish that it predated start-up.
There is no pre-start-up flow verification, and internal damage to V-001 could plausibly release loose material. No process data are supplied to exclude other damage mechanisms.
The HAZOP deviation covers errors in FWKO start-up procedures generally, not only the bypass line-up.
The reference possible-cause list is withheld, so other credible HAZOP causes cannot be ruled out.

candidate_causes.cause_description: The operator omitted the bypass-opening step before start-up (the shift supervisor's hypothesis). This is tenable only if both the time-stamped witness record and the checklist are erroneous.

evidence_against.relevance: A time-stamped witness record documents the operator moving the bypass-valve handle to the indicated open position before start-up. This directly contradicts omission.
The commissioning checklist records the bypass-opening step as completed.
The handle was found in the indicated open position after the event. A physical obstruction in the bypass path provides a non-operator explanation for the absent bypass flow.

evidence_for.relevance: V-001 was damaged after start-up and no independent verification of bypass flow exists. This is consistent with, but not specific to, a bypass that was not opened.
The HAZOP recognizes start-up procedure error as a credible deviation for V-001.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: HAZOP frame: node V-001 (CASE-01). Design intent: start-up with the bypass path open and flowing per the commissioning procedure. Deviation: start-up procedure error leaving no effective bypass flow at start-up (CASE-02). Consequence realized: internal damage to V-001 (CASE-03, E3). Safeguard: commissioning procedure (CASE-04), which did not prevent the event. Hypothesis test: operator omission is contradicted by three mutually consistent items. These are a time-stamped witness record of the operator moving the handle to open before start-up (E2), the checklist sign-off (E3), and the handle found in the open position after the event (E1). Omission is retained only as a residual (C4, 3%) that requires both the witness record and the checklist to be wrong. The same inspection found an internal obstruction in the bypass path (E1). This explains an ineffective bypass despite correct manual action, so a pre-existing mechanical blockage is the most defensible primary cause (C1, 57%). The safeguard verified the action (handle position and sign-off) rather than the outcome (actual flow). This latent procedural weakness allowed the blockage to go undetected (C2, 18%, contributing). A material alternative (C3, 22%) is that the obstruction is secondary debris or coincidental, and the damage arose from another undocumented start-up deviation. This cannot be excluded because the obstruction was found only after the event and no pre-start-up flow verification exists (E3). Qualitative risk: severity is realized internal equipment damage; no other consequence data are supplied. Likelihood cannot be ranked from the packet. The sole safeguard proved ineffective for this failure mode, so this should be treated as high priority pending formal ranking. Recommendations: (1) characterize the obstruction (composition, origin, condition of valve internals) to discriminate C1 from C3; (2) retrieve any start-up process records; (3) revise the commissioning procedure to require positive, independent verification of actual bypass flow before start-up instead of relying on handle position; (4) add pre-start-up inspection or flushing of the bypass line; (5) do not attribute the event to operator omission on current evidence.
uncertainty_notes: The timing and origin of the bypass obstruction are unresolved. E1 is a post-event finding, and E3 confirms there is no independent pre-start-up flow verification. The obstruction may therefore predate start-up (causal) or be debris from the damage (secondary).
The packet does not characterize the obstruction. It could be foreign material, construction debris, a valve internal failure, or fragments of V-001 internals.
The packet does not describe how an unavailable bypass would damage V-001 internals. No start-up process data (pressure, level, flow, differential pressure) are supplied.
The commissioning procedure content is not supplied. It is unknown whether the procedure required flow verification, or whether verification was performed but not recorded.
The source-derived HAZOP possible-cause list is withheld (CASE-05), so other reference causes for the start-up deviation cannot be cross-checked.
The witness's identity and independence behind E2 are not described. Rejection of the omission hypothesis rests on the record's time-stamp and its consistency with E1 and E3.
Plausibility percentages are relative judgment weights. C2 is a latent contributor that coexists with C1, not a mutually exclusive alternative.
The packet provides no risk-matrix categories, so the qualitative risk ranking is indicative only.
